original_value: AbstractNext-generation sequencing has paved the way for the reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic networks as a powerful tool for understanding metabolic circuits in any organism. However, the visualization and extraction of knowledge from these large networks comprising thousands of reactions and metabolites is a current challenge in need of user-friendly tools. Here we present Fluxer (https://fluxer.umbc.edu), a free and open-access novel web application for the computation and visualization of genome-scale metabolic flux networks. Any genome-scale model based on the Systems Biology Markup Language can be uploaded to the tool, which automatically performs Flux Balance Analysis and computes different flux graphs for visualization and analysis. The major metabolic pathways for biomass growth or for biosynthesis of any metabolite can be interactively knocked-out, analyzed and visualized as a spanning tree, dendrogram or complete graph using different layouts. In addition, Fluxer can compute and visualize the k-shortest metabolic paths between any two metabolites or reactions to identify the main metabolic routes between two compounds of interest. The web application includes >80 whole-genome metabolic reconstructions of diverse organisms from bacteria to human, readily available for exploration. Fluxer enables the efficient analysis and visualization of genome-scale metabolic models toward the discovery of key metabolic pathways.

result.paraphrase: AbstractNext-generation sequencing has enabled reconstruction of genome-scale metabolic networks, providing a powerful way to understand metabolic circuits in any organism. Yet visualizing and extracting knowledge from these large networks, which contain thousands of reactions and metabolites, remains a challenge that calls for user-friendly tools. We introduce Fluxer (https://fluxer.umbc.edu), a free and open-access web application for computing and visualizing genome-scale metabolic flux networks. Users can upload any genome-scale model in Systems Biology Markup Language format; the tool automatically runs Flux Balance Analysis and generates multiple flux graphs for analysis and visualization. Major metabolic pathways for biomass growth or for biosynthesis of any metabolite can be interactively knocked out, examined, and displayed as a spanning tree, dendrogram, or complete graph with different layouts. Fluxer can also compute and visualize the k-shortest metabolic paths between any two metabolites or reactions, helping identify the principal metabolic routes between two compounds of interest. The web application includes more than 80 whole-genome metabolic reconstructions from diverse organisms, ranging from bacteria to human, ready for exploration. Fluxer supports efficient analysis and visualization of genome-scale metabolic models to help discover key metabolic pathways.
